_comment: THE AGENTIC HARNESS layer. Owner, 2026-09-20: "cat-harness, folio-assistant-core, folio-assistant are distinct instances/schemas" — so this declares itself `cat-harness` rather than `folio-assistant`. It carried the latter until the repository root gained a harness.json of its own, at which point TWO instances declared one name and `instanceRoots` — keyed on the declared name — could only hold one of them. The one it held was the root, so `folio-assistant` resolved to the checkout and the harness layer became unreachable by name. `stub` is UNCHANGED and stays `folio-assistant`: the stub names the PUBLISHED artefact (docs/folio-assistant/, _kg/folio-assistant.jsonld, the Pages path) and the name names the instance, which is the entire reason a declaration carries both. The CatHarness declaration for THIS instance — what directories it scans and what kind of graph each holds. See skills/folio-core/directory-conventions.md. This repo is PRE-SPLIT (issue #223), so it declares what is true today, not the target layout: `tools/` and `folio/` do not exist here yet and are deliberately not declared. A directory that is declared but absent is worse than one that is missing, because every consumer then scans nothing and reports a clean run over it. NOTE: `schemas/` declares TWO graphs — the first real use of the array. A directory is a place to look and may hold more than one part of the graph; it does not say how to tell them apart, because the files declare what they are (see bean xxxb: schemas/*.ts does not yet do this well). `beans/` is declared ONCE, as a single `beans` graph. Its internal split — `defs` for work items, `workflows` for running BPMN state — is declared by `beans/beans.json`, not here. #263 declared the two as separate directories, one nested inside the other, which left a consumer unable to tell which owned what beneath it; the nodes now carry that.
_title: No `title`, deliberately: `displayTitle` is title || name || id, so the sidebar and the landing page fall back to `name` — which the schema already requires to be the instance's identifier, the one artefacts are stub-named after. A title here said `c@t-harness` and overrode that, labelling THIS repository with the brand of the harness layer that is still to be split out of it. Setting the title to `folio-assistant` instead would be the same fact in two fields, free to drift. The c@t-harness derivation stays in the description, where it is a tagline rather than an identity.
name: cat-harness
_title_comment: The HUMAN display name, for the LHS navbar's harness tabs. Owner, 2026-09-21: "harnesses should list the names (they should be named in schmeas, e.g. cat-boostrap should be named 'Boostrap', f-a => Folio Assistant, cat-harness => C@T Harness)". `name` stays the machine identifier that filenames, `needs` edges and `declaredBy` resolve against; `title` is what a reader sees and nothing resolves against. Bean t3n8. THIS ONE WAS WRONG RATHER THAN ABSENT: it declared `title: "folio-assistant"`, the ROOT instance's name, so two instances carried one title and `disambiguate()` correctly qualified this tab to "folio-assistant (cat-harness)" — the label the owner reported. The disambiguator behaved as designed; the declaration was the defect.

assets.title: AGENTS.md — cat-harness
assets.description: The cold-start file for an agent working IN this layer, and it is THIS LAYER'S own as of 2026-09-20 (issue #592). It was declared `scope: "repository"`, so it resolved to the repository root's AGENTS.md — one file answering both "what binds everywhere" and "what binds in the harness layer", which is the conflation `readmeFinding` calls MAJOR for a non-root instance and could not report, because the asset DID resolve. It resolved to the wrong file's job. No `source`: this file is authored here. The root's carries the bootstrap provenance, because the root's is the file bootstrap copies at initialisation.

assets.title: cat-harness
assets.description: What this LAYER is, for a reader — as distinct from what the repository is, which is the root's README. Split from it on 2026-09-20 (issue #592); before that this instance had no README of its own and claimed the repository's. It does not list this instance's directories: `harness.json` is that list, and a second copy in prose is free to disagree with it the day a directory moves.

assets.title: Initializing into folio-assistant
assets.description: What bootstrap's step 2 reads once it has been pointed at THIS instance. Published at the fixed convention every cat-harness instance honours, composed by `initializationDoc()` rather than spelled, so bootstrap needs no per-target knowledge and can initialise into a SPECIALISED harness it was never written against. Declared as an asset as well as conventional, so `check:declared-assets` verifies it is there and that its links resolve: a convention nothing checks is a convention that is honoured until it quietly is not. The path is INSTANCE-relative here, not `<stub>/docs/...`: this instance has its own directory (`cat-harness/`), so `siteDir` is plain `docs`, and the stub names published artefacts rather than a directory. Whether bootstrap can still find it from one reference is open — see bean `wggr`.

_stub_comment: RENAMED from `folio-assistant` on 2026-09-21, on the owner's ruling, closing the collision issue #649 raised and bean `x3bd` flagged as settle-before-you-move. `artefactStub(d) = d.stub ?? d.name`, so this field is the ONLY stub declared anywhere in the tree — every other instance falls through to its `name`. While it read `folio-assistant` it was the string the REPOSITORY ROOT instance also carries as its `name`, so both resolved to `<base>/folio-assistant.jsonld`: two vocabularies, one path, and a reader dereferencing it got whichever layer answered. It is kept as an explicit field rather than deleted so the rename is visible where the collision was, and because `x3bd` records that this string names published artefacts (`.jsonld`, `.schema.json`, the viewer directory) rather than being cosmetic.
_publication_comment: The `publication host` axis of docs/proposals/deployment-topologies.md, accepted 2026-09-19 (issue #363). WHAT KIND of host serves the renderings — distinct from `canonicalUrl` (the base @ids are minted against) and from `readme.linkStyle` in harness.config.json (how a link to a published artefact is written). This instance really does publish to GitHub Pages, so it declares so; an instance that has not said is `undefined`, which is a third state and must never be read as `github-pages`.

stickies._comment: ONE CARD FOR THIS HARNESS, per the owner's ruling of 2026-09-20: "not all stickies should be cat harness they should be outputs (as if) each init harness ran ... each own intiaization sticky note to show sucess". It replaces three — `landing`, `cat-harness` and `subgraphs`. The first two are merged here because they were always this one harness talking about itself twice; the third moved to folio-assist-core, whose subject content IS.  `bodyFrom: description` rather than a literal body, so the c@t-harness derivation chain is read from the declaration above and cannot drift from it — the owner: "dont lose acronym definitions". `bodyAppend` carries the cat's introduction and the scope line, which is why that field exists.  THEME `grumpy-cat`, the sage hoodie, per "cat-harness=gumpy hoddie".
stickies.summary: computable adjudication and agentic test harness
stickies.bodyAppend:
Please be introduced to a cat who acquires things, for whatever purpose — maybe somebody knows.

**Scope:** the platform — skills, schemas, processes, the MCP server and the pipeline. Not what a folio IS (that is folio-assist-core), and not any folio's own content, which lives in its own repository.

links.label: cat-harness, in the source
links.note: Still to be split out of this repository — issue #223.

links.label: RTFM — the cat-harness docs
links.note: The agent–user interaction model, and what this harness is for.

directories.description: Tool definitions, one subdirectory per contributing instance (tools/<stub>/) so a composed instance adds its own without colliding on a filename. tools/index.ts merges them and is the only path a consumer imports. Authored as .ts calling defineTool so a malformed node fails at tsc; the JSON-LD and JSON Schema renderings are generated.

The content-object model and the per-skill JSON Schemas. Declares BOTH graphs: the schema definitions themselves, and `kg` because a schema IS a knowledge-graph node — the .ts files are part of the KG, not a separate island beside it.

directories._comment: CAT-BOOTSTRAP'S RENDER SUBGRAPH, declared here for the same reason its sibling above is: `resolveSkillDirs` walks THIS instance's declaration plus its dependencies, and bootstrap is not a declared dependency of cat-harness — it is composed under it. So a directory declared only in `bootstrap/harness.json` is invisible to `skill_fetch` from this root, which is how bootstrap's own skills came to be declared twice BY DECISION (see the entry above). WITHOUT IT the two skills that constitute bootstrap's rendering exemption are unfetchable from the root — and an exemption whose substitute cannot be reached is the hole `renderExemption.owes` exists to close. Bean `hfkl`. A SEPARATE id from `bootstrap`, because overrides match on id and reusing it would replace the skills with these.

directories.description: The knowledge graph. Skill packages, and the four other node kinds that point at them: `roles/roles.json` (a role IS a BPMN swimlane, and carries the skills its lane's activities need), `workflows/*.bpmn` + `workflows/decisions/*.dmn` (the processes those roles act in, reached through the skill that describes them), `requirements/*.json` (conformance obligations whose `satisfiedBy` names the skill or capability discharging them), `permissions/permissions.json` (what an actor may DO in any lane, as opposed to what its lane's role knows), Its audit verdicts are NOT here: they moved to the `qa` tree on 2026-09-19, because a verdict is a QA reviewer's output and placement follows provenance. Note the id is `kg` while the path is `skills/` — ids are stable across a relocation, paths are not.

Scenarios — the Roles an Actor takes on, in `roles.json`. A Role IS a BPMN swimlane: it carries the Skills its lane's activities need, the lanes it binds, and the Actor kinds that may play it. SPLIT OUT OF `skills/` on 2026-09-21 so that "give me the Scenarios" is a query on the kind rather than a match on a path. One third of what this kind is named for is NOT here yet: a Role's `useCases` are free-text strings, so a User Story cannot be pointed at or traced to the Workflow it justifies.

Executable BPMN processes and the DMN tables their gateways compute from. The diagrams are the source of truth, not illustrations of one: a lane binds a Role, an activity names the Skill to run through `<folio:skill ref>`, and `workflow_complete` refuses a step that is not enabled. WHERE A RUNNING INSTANCE GOT TO is not here — that is `beans/workflows/`, kind `workflow-state`, which is `state` rather than `content`. Two questions, two graphs.

RACI as its own subgraph beside CRDM. Three declared edge kinds — accountable, consulted, informed — over the BPMN activities and `roles.json` entries that already exist, NOT a new party registry: a second table of names would be a second answer to `who is the reviewer`, free to disagree with the registry, which is the drift the retired skill `roles:` field cost 260 dangling values (bean qif9). R is deliberately absent because a lane already declares it. Owner, 2026-09-20, bean 7o7i: exactly one Accountable per activity, ENFORCED by `check:raci`.

CRDM as its OWN topical subgraph — its skills and its eight diagrams together, rather than three skills in folio-core and eight .bpmn in skills/workflows/ with nothing but a filename prefix relating them. Owner, 2026-09-20: CRDM, RACI, SDLC and MADR all live under `methodologies/`, each its own subgraph. I proposed a separate `workflow-methodologies/` on the reading that PROCESS methods (how a process runs) and JUDGEMENT methods (how to decide — Kepner-Tregoe, MADR, DMN) are different axes; the owner settled it as ONE tree, which is the better answer for the reason this repository keeps relearning: two directories whose boundary needs a paragraph to explain are two answers to `where do methodologies live`, and the next author picks the wrong one. This is the layout `skillMdDirs` was built for: its own comment names `crdm` as the example of a topical directory that should cost a declaration line and no code change, and `bootstrap/skills/` was the first such root. Each methodology is declared SEPARATELY rather than declaring the parent, because `workflowDirs` resolves `<kgdir>/workflows` — declaring only the parent would leave every diagram undiscovered. SDLC and RACI are deliberately NOT declared until they have content: a declared-but-absent directory is the `dh4f` defect.

CRDM's own executable processes — the eight BPMN diagrams that RUN the requirements methodology rather than describe it. Declared as `workflows` on 2026-09-21 for the same reason `skills/workflows/` is: before the split these sat inside a `cat-harness` directory and were reached by convention, and the moment the parent became `skills` the processes index pruned them as an orphan. A diagram's kind follows what the FILE is, not which methodology owns the directory above it.

Judgement methodologies the harness owns, one sub-graph each: Kepner-Tregoe for a decision, MADR for its record, DMN for the computable case. PARALLEL rather than composable — which applies is contextual, and blending them produces a house method that cites nobody. Its own graph kind rather than skills, for three properties a skill does not have: extractable (somebody else's work, adopted, so it lifts out with its declaration when the field moves on), referenced rather than inlined (two skills quoting one method is two copies free to drift), and exempt from skill criteria (skill-is-brief caps an INSTRUCTION near 280 lines; a methodology is a faithful rendering of an external standard, and truncating it to fit a house limit would misrepresent the standard). GRADE is deliberately NOT here — see smart-kg-methodologies.

Everything a QA process produced, in one declared tree. The owner's rule, 2026-09-19: an artefact generated primarily as a QA reviewer belongs under `test/results/` as part of a QA process — placement follows PROVENANCE, not file family and not who fetches it afterwards. Three kinds live here and the FILES say which they are, per the `$schema` contract: `qa-results/v1` (`<producer>.qa-results.json`, a whole-artefact review — findings about a document the build just produced), `qa-witness/v1` (`witnesses/**`, one per audited subject in the families `block`, `kg` and `translation`, the published projection) and `kg-qa/v1` (`kg-qa/**`, the KG verdicts themselves — what `kg-audit` wrote). The `kg-qa/` tree MIRRORS each subject's path rather than being flat, and that is not tidiness: measured 2026-09-19, four sidecar basenames already occur twice across packages (`editor`, `getting-started`, `idle-backlog`, `l2-dak-authoring`), so a flat directory would silently overwrite four verdicts. `kgQaSidecarPath` in `schemas/kg-qa.ts` is the one answer for writer and reader alike. A directory is a PLACE TO LOOK and may hold more than one part of a graph; extension is a coincidence, a declaration inside the file is the contract. ONE entry rather than a nested set, deliberately: #263's own comment names the defect a declaration inside another declaration creates. STILL OUTSIDE: the 122 block verdicts `*.qa.json`, which sit beside their blocks and move next. The witnesses are PUBLISHED at `/assets/qa/`, which is where every badge points; the publishing workflows copy them into `_site/assets/qa/` after Jekyll, since Jekyll builds only `docs/`. Where a file lives and where it is served from are different questions.

The trashcan that is kept. Deprecated and throwaway structured content — addressable, exported as <base>/fsh-guts.jsonld, and DELIBERATELY absent from the rendered site. Every other declared kind here is non-renderable because it is a graph a tool reads and there was never a page to make of it; this one's contents could be rendered and are not, so that something can be kept without being published. It is also the destination that makes the never-delete rule enforceable beyond beans: AGENTS.md forbids deleting a bean because a scrapped item stops the next agent re-entering a dead end while a deleted one cannot be told from an accident, and that reasoning was always general — an agent removing a page or a script had only `rm`. Delete now means relocate here, and relocate is reversible. Files declare themselves with `$schema: folio-fsh-guts/v1`, per the same contract the bean and workflow stores use. NOTE on the name: `.fsh` is FHIR Shorthand in this codebase and across the WHO SMART folios; the collision was raised and the owner confirmed this spelling. REPOSITORY-scoped: it sits at the top of the checkout, not inside this instance, and it is deliberately never overlaid by a dependency.

Repository health reports — what the daily sweep under `test/health/` wrote. One `health-report/v1` document, declaring itself with a `$schema` tag rather than being duck-typed by path: a directory is a PLACE TO LOOK and the files inside say what they are. A SEPARATE graph from `qa`, and the line between them is about the SUBJECT, not the producer: a QA verdict judges an artefact this repository produced, against criteria that artefact is supposed to meet; a health report judges the REPOSITORY ITSELF — how big it has grown, how much of the publish branch the review previews occupy, whether the work plan has duplicates in it. Folding it into `qa` would leave a consumer asking for verdicts about this instance's content holding a fact about its clone. NOTE the path: it was `tests/health/results/` when this graph landed in #395, because this repository then had BOTH `test/` (the `qa` graph) and `tests/` (the Playwright e2e specs), and the owner asked for `tests/health`. #395 flagged that inconsistency in `skills/folio-core/directory-conventions.md` rather than resolving it, since relocating a declared directory as a side effect of adding a check is the `dh4f` shape, where a consumer scans nothing and reports a clean run over it. The owner settled it on `test/` the same day and it moved as its own change — bean `auap`, PR #400. The `id` here is unchanged, deliberately: an inheriting instance overrides on the entry's id and never on its path, so `health` still binds after the relocation. The e2e specs came to the declaration rather than the declaration to the specs, because `testDir` is one line of one config file and a declared path is what every downstream override resolves against.

The work plan. `beans/beans.json` declares its nodes — `defs` (work items) and `workflows` (running BPMN instance state). REPOSITORY-scoped: it sits at the top of the checkout, not inside this instance, and it is deliberately never overlaid by a dependency.

A PERSON's outstanding items — the human half of memory, as against `beans/`, which is the agent's workflow management. Not a second work plan: the two sit in different quadrants of one 2x2 (memory vs workflow management, human vs agent), and human workflow management is EMPTY, deliberately. `todos/todos.json` declares its nodes — `items` (raised about anything) and `feedback` (raised against a specific block, carrying the submitter's identity) — the same shape as `beans/beans.json`. REPOSITORY-scoped: it sits at the top of the checkout, not inside this instance, and it is deliberately never overlaid by a dependency.

Agent memory — durable facts an agent carries between sessions, one `"$schema": "folio-memory/v1"` node each, assembled into `.claude/agent-memory/<agent>/MEMORY.md`. `context` by the axis bean `mhh9` settled: read during a process, never written by one; it changes when a human directs an authoring agent. It sat in `skills/memory/` until 2026-09-20 — inside the `cat-harness` directory, which is `content` — so the CONTAINING kind and the contents were on opposite layers, and a nested declaration is the defect #263 names. Moving it was held back from the classification change on purpose (#395's rule, and bean `auap`'s precedent: a relocation is its own change) and is bean `07xs`. SCOPE IS `repository`, like `beans/`: these are facts about this REPOSITORY carried by the agents working in it, and `.claude/agents/` — the consumers — sit at the repository root too.

How a PERSON wants to be asked — committed, read at session start by every agent. `context` by the same test as agent memory: read during a process, never written by one, changed when a person states a preference. It sat in `.harness/`, undeclared, until 2026-09-20, which this repository's own dot-prefix guard forbids: a dot-prefixed directory is absent from a plain `ls`, from most file browsers and from a forge's web tree, and the file read at the start of every session was in the one place the conventions reject. The path is also `harness.config.json`'s `interaction` key, which defaults here — the declaration and the config now name the same place instead of one of them being a literal nobody checks. SCOPE IS `repository`, and omitting it was a live defect for an hour on 2026-09-20: without it the path resolves against the INSTANCE, so a consumer looked in `cat-harness/` while the content sat at the repository root — and `harness:dirs` then created the empty instance-level directory to satisfy the declaration, turning declared-but-absent into declared-and-empty, which is the `dh4f` false pass wearing a tidier face. Repository, not instance, for the same reason `beans/` and `todos/` are: these are read by every agent working in this repository, not by this instance's code.

How far an agent has read an issue: `lastCommentId`, `lastUpdatedAt` and `checkedAt`, one file per issue. NOT the comments — the marks say what was seen, and one of the two files here says so in its own note. Two marks rather than one because a comment EDITED after being read keeps its id, so the id alone would call it seen and an edited requirement is a changed requirement (`issue-working`). `state`: a running process writes one each time it checks. Moved out of `.harness/issue-comments/` on 2026-09-20 for the reason `.beans/` and `.harness/workflow/` moved on 2026-09-18 — the artefacts a person looks for first were the hardest to find. SCOPE IS `repository`, and omitting it was a live defect for an hour on 2026-09-20: without it the path resolves against the INSTANCE, so a consumer looked in `cat-harness/` while the content sat at the repository root — and `harness:dirs` then created the empty instance-level directory to satisfy the declaration, turning declared-but-absent into declared-and-empty, which is the `dh4f` false pass wearing a tidier face. Repository, not instance, for the same reason `beans/` and `todos/` are: these are read by every agent working in this repository, not by this instance's code.

The incoming queue of the document-ingestion pipeline — raw files as dropped, before ingestion. NOT L1 and NOT greppable as corpus: the corpus checklist searches library/ only, so a source still sitting here reads as absent to every consumer while the file is on disk. That is why it is a separate declaration from library/ rather than the same directory under two names.

L1 source content — one `<bib-slug>/` per ingested document, holding `sections/*.md`, `structure.json` and, where the source was scanned, `ocr/page-NNN.txt`. THIS INSTANCE HOLDS NONE. Bean `frs5` moved all four entries out (the three IRIS items to who-iris, milnorlink to folio-assistant-sci) because the platform holds no content, and this entry was removed with them. It is back, on the owner's ruling of 2026-09-20, for ONE reason and it is not about this instance: `wwi6` pins the guarantee that a DEPENDENT folio materialises its own `uploads/` and `library/`, and a dependent inherits the convention — an id and a relative path — from what the harness declares. Remove this and every downstream folio silently stops getting a library. IT IS THE `dh4f` SHAPE AND THAT IS KNOWN, NOT OVERLOOKED: a declared directory this instance does not hold is exactly what that bean is about. The cost is paid deliberately and it is bounded — the consumers that scan libraries now fan out over EVERY declared one (bean `a02m`), so an empty one contributes nothing rather than shadowing the two that have content. What it must never become again is the FIRST of several silently taken as the only one. The real fix is the core relocation — `uploads`, `voices`, `translation-sources` and this moving to folio-assistant-core, per the owner's earlier "voices, uploads library in folio-asst-core" — after which a dependent inherits them from the layer that owns content and this entry goes for good.

The WHO IRIS instance's library, reached from here because this repository STAGES who-iris as a sibling top-level directory ahead of it becoming its own repo -- the same pattern as `folio-assist-core-schemas` and `detangle-schemas` above. Repository-scoped, so it resolves against the repository root rather than this instance's. Declared here as well as in who-iris/harness.json because the consumers that scan libraries -- `check:l1-complete`, the narrative queue, `gen-library-jsonld`, the MCP server's graph roots -- run from THIS root, and a library they cannot see is a corpus they report a clean pass over (the dh4f defect).

The agent-skill literature instance's library -- published guidance on authoring and operating agent skills, vendor documentation and arXiv papers alike. Same staging arrangement and same reason as `who-iris-library` and `folio-assistant-sci-library` below: the consumers that scan libraries run from THIS root, and a library they cannot see is a corpus they report a clean pass over (the dh4f defect). It is NOT in cat-harness/library/ although its subject is this harness's own: `AGENTS.md` opens by saying the platform holds no content, and these are other publishers' documents.

The science instance's library -- `milnorlink`, and nothing else. Same staging arrangement and same reason as `who-iris-library` above. Bean r1lz sent it here rather than to who-iris: it is not an IRIS item and never was.

Editorial voice profiles — named rule sets overlaid on the base house voice, one JSON per voice. A voice is a THIRD axis beside adapters (which partition block kinds) and profiles (which partition what a folio may contain): it partitions how prose reads. Opt-in: this instance ships four and activates none, because folio-assistant's own documentation carries no voice (issue #208).

The gettext side of translation — one directory per target locale holding `.pot` templates, `.po` catalogues and the `TranslationNode` `.ts` manifests that make each pair addressable in the graph. The INPUT to injection. There is deliberately NO matching declaration for the rendered OUTPUT: a translated page is the same kind of thing as the page it translates — renderable content, differing by a field — and it declares its own `lang` and `translation_source` in front matter, so the locale subtrees under `docs/` are DISCOVERED from the files rather than enumerated here. A first draft of PR #351 enumerated them, ten entries for five locales across two subtrees, and that restated what all ten files already said. Undeclared until 2026-09-19: the `dh4f` defect in reverse, five committed directories that no declaration mentioned.

Authored content of this instance itself, rendered to a website. Holds the landing sticky — the instance's own description and its onboarding links, as a page-global note rather than text composited into the backdrop.

GRADE, and the first content in smart-kg. Certainty-of-evidence grading belongs to WHO L1 guideline development rather than to an agent framework: a folio formalising mathematics has evidence and no use for GRADE. Separated so the extraction is literal — smart-kg/ lifts out whole — which is the layout #223 asks for and bootstrap/ already demonstrates, and it is why this path is repository-scoped, like the bootstrap entry, rather than instance-relative. It has a slot waiting rather than needing one built: evidence-retrieval.bpmn runs Task_AppraiseGrade against "the grading system the folio declares", and its own documentation calls that a STRAWPERSON. Adopting the method as a sub-graph keeps the slot pluggable instead of wiring one system into the diagram.

Documentation ABOUT the knowledge graph itself -- 241 markdown files, the entire published surface, and UNDECLARED until 2026-09-20. That is the dh4f defect in its purest form: every declaration-driven consumer scanned straight past the thing readers actually see. Owner, same day: 'docs/ is about documentation about the KG itself... docs/ in cat-harness', with the intent that this is WHERE DOCUMENTATION GOES and therefore the only place a forward reference may be authored. The `docs` kind is RENDERABLE and is registered by `schemas/docs-graph-kind.ts` rather than added to BASE_GRAPH_KINDS, so the assertion that the harness's base vocabulary carries no renderable kind stays true and its test stays unchanged. Distinct from `folio`, which is core's: the difference is the SUBJECT. A page explaining how ingestion works is `docs`; a note an author writes about an ingested catalogue is a `folio`; the catalogue itself is `library/`. `dependents` is `skip`, unlike the other renderable graph `folio`: this is documentation THIS instance publishes about the knowledge graph, so a dependent folio inherits the pages rather than an empty directory to refill — it authors its own subject matter under `folio/`, which is `reproduce`. CHANGED TO `reproduce` 2026-09-21 ON THE OWNER'S COMPOSE RULING (bean `n0nf`, issue #638), and the paragraph above is kept rather than deleted because its reasoning was right for the question it answered. It argued `skip` on the grounds that a dependent should INHERIT THE PAGES rather than get an empty directory to refill. Under compose it gets BOTH: the pages still reach it, and `reproduce` gives it the place to override one. So this is not a reversal of that argument, it is the second half of it arriving. The `dependents` doc warns that defaulting to `reproduce` ships junk -- twelve inherited directories, four of them the platform's own, each empty with a committed keep marker, the `dh4f` shape shipped downstream. That warning is about a DEFAULT, and the test it turns on is the one that schema states: is this directory part of the SHAPE a folio has, or merely where THIS instance's content lives? Before the ruling `docs/` was the second. After it, a folio is expected to author and override its own documentation, which makes it the first -- the same answer `uploads/` and `library/` get, and they are `reproduce` and also start empty. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO is give the REPOSITORY ROOT a `docs/`. The root does not depend on cat-harness (measured: its declaration chain has length 1), so nothing is inherited there, and the root's own `harness.json` carries the owner's "only uploads/ on this repo's root". `n0nf` says the root's docs "is not its own: cat-harness installs it", which needs a dependency edge that does not exist. That is left for the owner rather than settled here.

THE REPOSITORY ROOT'S DOCUMENTATION OVERLAY, managed by this instance. Owner's ruling, 2026-09-21, answering whether the root declares its own docs: "harness can have docs/ which then get listed under cat-harness/docs/<harness>, there is also docs/ dir in repo root managed by cat-harness. other harness augment or overlay ontop of that (content and behviors)". SEPARATE FROM THE `docs` ENTRY ABOVE, AND IT HAS TO BE. That one is instance-scoped and `reproduce`, which is what makes a DEPENDENT materialise its own docs/ (bean n0nf slice 1). This one is `scope: "repository"`, and a repository-scoped entry is filtered out for dependencies -- cat-harness.ts:3261 and :3507 both skip it unless `link.own`. Re-scoping the existing entry instead of adding this one would therefore have UNDONE slice 1 silently: a dependent would simply stop getting a docs/ and nothing would fail. Two directories answering two questions, so two entries, with distinct ids -- the convention `who-iris-docs` already follows. `dependents` is `skip` for the same reason every other cross-instance repository-scoped entry here is: a dependent never reaches this one at all, and claiming it reproduces would be a promise the resolver does not keep. WHAT MAKES IT NOT `dh4f`: a declared directory that nothing reads is this repository's most-paid-for defect, and an empty overlay is exactly that shape. It is consumed by the site build, which composes it OVER cat-harness/docs/ -- so what it contributes today is nothing VERIFIABLY, pinned by a test asserting an empty overlay produces a byte-identical site, rather than nothing unnoticed.

The CONTENT layer's schema nodes, staged as a top-level directory ahead of the split (#223). Owner, 2026-09-20: 'not in cat-harness, in folio-assitant-core/ as a named subgraph.' A NAMED SUBGRAPH and not a second `schemas` entry: overrides match on the entry's id, so reusing `schemas` would REPLACE this instance's schema graph rather than add to it -- the same trap the `cat-harness-src` entry above documents from the other side. REPOSITORY-scoped, like `bootstrap/skills/`: it sits at the top of the checkout, not inside this instance, and is deliberately never overlaid by a dependency. This entry is the mirror of `folio-assistant-core/harness.json`'s own, and it has to be stated twice only because `resolveSkillDirs` has no caller -- when that is wired, THIS entry is the one to delete.

The TOOLED knowledge-graph navigation skill, lifted out of the `folio-core` package on 2026-09-20 at the owner's direction: '(kg-navigation should be similar named subgraph)'. Repository-scoped and a SIBLING of `skills/`, not a child: `skills/` is already declared as this instance's `cat-harness` graph in full, so a nested entry would be a declaration inside a declaration -- #263's own defect, where a consumer beneath the outer path cannot tell which declaration owns what it finds. The name is shared with `bootstrap/skills/kg-navigation.md`, which stays where it is and must: that one assumes NOTHING is installed, and a bootstrap reaching into another instance for its first skill would fail in the cold-start case it exists for. Two bodies under one name, each addressable -- see kg-navigation/README.md.

The `large-datasets` subgraph's instruction bodies. Declared here as well as in its own harness.json for the same reason kg-navigation is: `resolveSkillDirs` has no caller yet, so a nested instance's directories are not reachable from the root. `materialize-remote` lives here and is named by two diagrams in cat-harness/skills/workflows/ -- a skill ref resolves across the declared graphs, not within one directory.

The who-iris instance's skills. ONE today -- `iris-dspace`, how IRIS uses DSpace and qualified Dublin Core, and what a later tool needs from a record stated as checkable requirements. Deliberately thin, per the owner's 'mionimal tools in who specific stuff': the Dublin Core TYPE is generic and lives in folio-assist-core, the enumeration/subsetting descriptor lives in large-datasets, and OCR stays a cat-harness platform tool. What is WHO-specific is only how IRIS uses those things.

The `large-datasets` subgraph's schema nodes -- `source-descriptor` (how to enumerate a corpus and ask it for a subset) and `artifact-store` (where an artifact too large for the site tree goes, as a declaration rather than a hardcoded host). Repository-scoped, so the path resolves against the REPO ROOT and carries no `../` -- a `../` prefix resolved OUTSIDE the checkout and every consumer silently dropped the entry (caught by CI, 2026-09-20).

The detangle criterion's schema node -- size, cohesion, inbound/outbound and the enforced/recorded edge authority that decides whether a boundary's direction is a fact or a filing decision. Repository-scoped, staged ahead of the split. UNDECLARED until 2026-09-20 although committed days earlier, which is the dh4f defect in reverse: graph content no declaration mentioned, so every declaration-driven consumer scanned past it -- including `check:schema-nodes`, the gate whose whole job is to stop a schema being silently absent.

The Zod that bootstrap's two published JSON Schemas are GENERATED from. Declared here AND in bootstrap-tools/harness.json, for the reason the sibling detangle/kg-navigation/large-datasets entries give: a directory declared only in an instance that is not a DEPENDENCY of this one is invisible from this root, because resolution walks this declaration plus its dependencies and bootstrap-tools is composed under the repository rather than depended on. Without this entry the schema graph reads 113 modules across four instances and bootstrap-tools contributes nothing — which is exactly the state this instance was created to end, since bootstrap itself contributed 0 of 113. The duplicate goes when the composition is wired, with the others.

_cat_bootstrap_comment: NO `bootstrap` DIRECTORY IS DECLARED HERE, and that is the owner's ruling of 2026-09-21 ("neither") on bean `pve3`, not an omission. This file used to declare `bootstrap/skills/` with `scope: "repository"`, which resolves against the REPOSITORY root rather than this instance — so bootstrap's skills and roles landed in folio-assistant's graph while the entry lived here. It did NOT declare `bootstrap/workflows/`, deliberately, because #432 measured bootstrap's process leaking into the root graph 88 times. The root therefore carried HALF of bootstrap, and the two symptoms were one asymmetry: a `lanes` entry on a bootstrap role minted `bindsLane -> role/<Lane>` pointing at a lane node only bootstrap's own export mints (four dangling links, measured 2026-09-21 by restoring `lanes` and watching `kg-export.test.ts` refuse it), and bootstrap's `kg-navigation` collided by name with `skills/folio-core/kg-navigation` in the published docs (bean `v3se`). `pve3` put the choice as BOTH halves or NEITHER; both would undo #432's isolation and put a process the root does not own into its published graph. Under NEITHER, bootstrap's skills are published through `bootstrap.jsonld` and its own instance page, which is where an instance's own graph belongs. The old entry's rationale is preserved in the bean rather than here, because a rationale for a declaration that no longer exists reads as a declaration to a skimming reader.
